system:
You audit the knowledge atoms of one Knowledge Card. A card is the answer key for a benchmark of expert conceptual knowledge, so every atom must be correct, self-contained, and assessable on its own.

Judge every atom on every check listed below. Rules:
- For checks about evidence, use only the evidence sentences supplied with the atom. Do not repair an atom with your own knowledge.
- For GROUNDED, use "hold" when unreadable PDF symbols prevent verification; explain what is needed. Use fail only when the available evidence is sufficient to determine that the claim is unsupported. This hold rule takes precedence over the strictness rule. Judge other checks independently using their listed values; do not invent missing facts.
- Be strict within each check's allowed values. Do not turn an inability to verify GROUNDED into revise or fail; use hold as defined above.
- "why" is required for every value other than the first listed value; keep it under 30 words. Omit "why" when passing.

Checks (allowed values in brackets; the first value means no problem):
- GROUNDED [pass / revise / fail / hold]: The cited evidence sentences state the atom, including its specificity, causal force, assumptions, and certainty. pass = fully stated. revise = partly stated (the atom adds, drops, or strengthens something; say what). fail = not stated when the available evidence permits a judgment. hold = unreadable symbols prevent verification. For pass or revise, put the supporting evidence ids in cite.
- SINGLE_CLAIM [pass / revise]: The atom is one independently assessable claim. revise = it joins two or more claims that could be true or false separately. Evidence spanning more than three sentences is not by itself a reason to split or revise an atom.
- SCOPE_LABEL [pass / revise]: The S label fits (S1 what it is / S2 how it works / S3 where it ends). revise = wrong label; put the right one in why, e.g. 'S2: ...'.
- L1_ONLY [pass / fail]: The atom is recall-level knowledge. fail = knowing it requires applying the concept to a new problem, or combining facts from distant passages.
- SOURCE_INDEPENDENT [pass / revise / fail]: A domain expert who never read this book could judge the claim true or false. revise = phrased as the authors' statement but the claim itself is general (drop the attribution). fail = an isolated study finding, conjecture, or author-specific opinion, classification, or recommendation, even if attribution was removed. Explicitly scoped established facts about a formalism or architecture and conditional theoretical results remain eligible.
- NO_OVERLAP [pass / fail]: No other atom in this card states or contains the same claim. If two atoms overlap, fail only the less informative one and put the other atom's id in cite; the other one passes.
- CENTRALITY [pass / fail]: The atom matters for understanding the concept. fail = peripheral detail.
Whole-card checks (report under "batch"):
- CONCEPT_SCOPE [pass / fail]: The concept is a general concept of the field. fail = a topic whose assessable content is restricted to excluded study-specific findings or author-specific positions. A named formalism, system, or architecture is not disqualified solely for being specific if its scoped conceptual facts are source-independent.

Output ONLY one JSON object:
{"units": {"<atom_id>": {"<CHECK>": {"v": "<value>", "why": "", "cite": []}, ...}, ...}, "batch": {"<CHECK>": {"v": "<value>", "why": ""}}}
user:
CONCEPT: Anodyne morphism
ASSESSMENT SCOPE: Cover anodyne morphisms of simplicial sets through their lifting definition, saturation by horn inclusions, retracts of cellular maps, and small-object factorization. Distinguish ordinary, inner, left and right versions and the hypotheses of the supplied generalized-horn recognition examples; exclude dendroidal anodyne maps and later model structures.

ATOMS:
- MATH-TOP-C07-S1-01 | S1
  ATOM: An inner, left, or right anodyne morphism of simplicial sets is defined as a morphism that has the left lifting property with respect to all inner, left, or right fibrations, respectively.
  EVIDENCE:
    [MATH-TOP-p0190-s22] Similarly, an inner, left, or right anodyne morphism is a morphism having the left lifting property with respect to inner, left, or right ﬁbrations, respectively.
- MATH-TOP-C07-S1-02 | S1
  ATOM: The class of inner anodyne morphisms contains all inner horn inclusions $\Lambda^k[n]\to\Delta[n]$ with $0<k<n$, and the other kinds of anodyne morphisms contain the corresponding horn inclusions in the same way.
  EVIDENCE:
    [MATH-TOP-p0191-s02] Thus the class of inner anodyne morphisms in particular contains all inner horn inclusions Λk[n] →∆[n], 0 < k < n, and similarly for the other kinds of anodynes.
- MATH-TOP-C07-S2-01 | S2
  ATOM: A map of simplicial sets is anodyne if and only if it is a retract of an $\mathcal{I}$-cellular map, where $\mathcal{I}$ is the set of horn inclusions $\Lambda^k[n]\to\Delta[n]$, and the analogous statement holds for inner, left, and right anodyne maps with the corresponding horn inclusions.
  EVIDENCE:
    [MATH-TOP-p0191-s17] Lemma 5.20 A map f : A →B of simplicial sets is anodyne if and only it is a retract of an I-cellular map, with I the set of horn inclusions Λk[n] →∆[n].
    [MATH-TOP-p0191-s18] Similarly it is inner, left, or right anodyne if and only if it is a retract of a map which is cellular with respect to inner, left, or right horn inclusions respectively.
- MATH-TOP-C07-S2-02 | S2
  ATOM: By the small object argument, with $\mathcal{I}$ the set of all horn inclusions $\Lambda^k[n]\to\Delta[n]$, any morphism $f:X\to Y$ of simplicial sets factors as $X\xrightarrow{i}Z\xrightarrow{p}Y$ with $i$ an $\mathcal{I}$-cellular map and $p$ a Kan fibration, and the analogous statement holds for inner, left, and right horns and fibrations.
  EVIDENCE:
    [MATH-TOP-p0191-s12] Lemma 5.19 Let I be the set of all horn inclusions Λk[n] →∆[n].
    [MATH-TOP-p0191-s13] Then any mor- phism f : X →Y of simplicial sets can be factored as
    [MATH-TOP-p0191-s14] X i−→Z p−→Y,
    [MATH-TOP-p0191-s15] with i an I-cellular map and p a Kan ﬁbration.
    [MATH-TOP-p0191-s16] The analogous statement is true for inner, left, or right horns and inner, left, or right ﬁbrations respectively.
- MATH-TOP-C07-S2-03 | S2
  ATOM: The class of anodyne morphisms (and likewise of inner, left, or right anodyne morphisms) is the smallest saturated class containing the corresponding horn inclusions.
  EVIDENCE:
    [MATH-TOP-p0192-s03] Corollary 5.21 The class of (inner, left, or right) anodyne maps is the smallest saturated class containing the (inner, left, or right) horn inclusions.
- MATH-TOP-C07-S3-01 | S3
  ATOM: For a non-empty subset $E\subset\{0,\dots,n\}$, the inclusion $\Lambda^E[n]\to\Delta[n]$ is anodyne in general, inner anodyne if $E\subseteq\{1,\dots,n-1\}$, left anodyne if $E\subseteq\{0,\dots,n-1\}$, and right anodyne if $E\subseteq\{1,\dots,n\}$.
  EVIDENCE:
    [MATH-TOP-p0193-s11] Lemma 5.23 Let E ⊂{0, . . ., n} be a non-empty subset and let ΛE[n] ⊆∆[n] be the union of all the faces ∂i∆[n] for i not in E; or, to put it more positively, the union of those faces containing all the vertices in E.
    [MATH-TOP-p0193-s13] (i) ΛE[n] →∆[n] is an anodyne morphism, (ii) ΛE[n] →∆[n] is inner anodyne if E ⊆{1, . . ., n −1}, (iii) ΛE[n] →∆[n] is left anodyne if E ⊆{0, . . ., n −1}, (iv) ΛE[n] →∆[n] is right anodyne if E ⊆{1, . . ., n}.
- MATH-TOP-C07-S3-02 | S3
  ATOM: A simplicial subset $A\subseteq\Delta[n]$ that is neither $\Delta[n]$ nor $\partial\Delta[n]$ and has the property that whenever $F_1,\dots,F_k$ are codimension 1 faces of $\Delta[n]$ not contained in $A$ the intersection $F_1\cap\cdots\cap F_k$ is also not contained in $A$, equals $\Lambda^E[n]$ for some non-empty $E\subseteq\{0,\dots,n\}$.
  EVIDENCE:
    [MATH-TOP-p0194-s09] Lemma 5.24 Consider a simplicial subset A ⊆∆[n].
    [MATH-TOP-p0194-s10] Suppose A is not equal to ∆[n] or ∂∆[n] and satisﬁes the following condition: if F1, . . ., Fk are codimension 1 faces of ∆[n] not contained in A, then also
    [MATH-TOP-p0194-s11] F1 ∩· · · ∩Fk ⊈A.
    [MATH-TOP-p0194-s12] Then A is equal to ΛE[n] for some nonempty subset E ⊆{0, . . ., n}.
- MATH-TOP-C07-S3-03 | S3
  ATOM: The inclusion $\Delta[1]\to J=N(0\leftrightarrow 1)$ given by the arrow $0\to1$ is both left anodyne and right anodyne.
  EVIDENCE:
    [MATH-TOP-p0192-s12] The arrow 0 →1 in this groupoid deﬁnes a morphism of simplicial sets ∆[1] →J.
    [MATH-TOP-p0192-s13] Proposition 5.22 The morphism ∆[1] →J is both left and right anodyne.
